title: 1952 AHSME Problem 25
statement: A powderman set a fuse for a blast to take place in \(30\) seconds. He ran away at a rate of \(8\) yards per second. Sound travels at the rate of \(1080\) feet per second. When the powderman heard the blast, he had run approximately:

solutions.text:
Let \(T\) be the total time in seconds. The powderman is \(8T\) yards, or \(24T\) feet, from the blast. Because the sound starts after \(30\) seconds, \[ 1080(T-30)=24T. \] Thus \(T=\frac{1350}{44}\) seconds, and the distance he ran is \[ 8T=\frac{2700}{11}\approx245.45\text{ yards}. \]

Approximately \(245\) yards is the listed value, so the correct answer is D.
hints: Let \(T\) be the total number of seconds from lighting the fuse until the sound is heard
At time \(T\), the sound has traveled for \(T-30\) seconds and must cover the runner’s distance
